title: Energy & Sustainability: Calculations
welcome_lead: Calculate efficiency, payback periods and capacity factors for real energy systems.
meta_desc: GCSE Environmental Science adventure on energy calculations: efficiency, payback period, capacity factor.
final_note: Energy maths unlocked. You can size a system from scratch.

concepts.def: Photovoltaic cells convert sunlight directly into electricity via the photoelectric effect.
Turbines convert kinetic energy of wind into electricity; offshore arrays are increasingly common.
Generates electricity from flowing or falling water; world's largest renewable source today.
Uses heat from Earth's interior to generate electricity or heat buildings (e.g., Iceland).
Captures kinetic and potential energy of tides; predictable but site-limited.
Burning organic matter (wood, crops, waste) for energy; carbon-neutral if regrown sustainably.

walkthroughs.body_html: Efficiency = (useful energy out / total energy in) x 100 percent. A coal plant turning 100 MJ of fuel into 35 MJ of electricity has 35 percent efficiency. Modern gas turbines reach about 60 percent. Combined heat and power (CHP) systems can exceed 80 percent by capturing waste heat for buildings.

Payback period = initial cost / annual savings. A 6000 pound solar PV system saving 600 pounds per year has a 10 year payback. After that, savings are net gain. Shorter payback is more attractive financially. Government subsidies, fuel price changes and degradation all affect real payback.

Capacity factor = actual energy generated / maximum possible if running at full power 24/7. UK onshore wind averages around 30 to 40 percent, offshore 40 to 50 percent, and solar PV 10 to 12 percent. A 1 MW turbine at 40 percent capacity produces 1 x 0.40 x 8760 = 3504 MWh per year.
